info.title: Task service
info.description:
The Task Service gives applications a means for defining and managing tasks, and managing work assignments.
A task is a _unit of work_ that is assigned to an individual for completion by a certain date.  Exactly what the unit of work is
depends on the feature the application is trying to implement, but can be such things as:
- response required,
- signature required,
- actions to be completed,
- etc.

You can combine tasks into  a _queue_ of work units that represents:
- a specific job to be completed by one or more individuals,
- an individual's daily workload,
- reminders for a user,
- etc.

Tasks and queues reside within _namespaces_, like a domain. A namespace might represent an application,
a specific workflow, or even an end-user role.  A well chosen namespace name can help ensure you're working
on the same tasks across an application or applications.

get.description: Retrieves the queues configured for the tenant. Available to any authenticated user of the tenant; no task service role is required. Core users must set the tenantId parameter.
Retrieves a specified queue of the tenant. Available to any authenticated user of the tenant; no task service role is required. Core users must set the tenantId parameter.

Retrieves the users of the tenant's Keycloak realm that hold one of the assigner roles of the queue. No task service role is required, but the request is made to the Keycloak admin API with the caller's token, so the user must hold the realm-management roles to view users (view-users) and, for client roles, clients (view-clients). Responds 403 if Keycloak denies the request. Roles that don't exist in the realm are skipped.

Retrieves task counts for a specified queue of the tenant, and optionally duration and rate metrics from the value service. Requires the task-admin or task-reader role, or one of the worker or assigner roles of the queue. Core users with one of those roles can retrieve metrics using the tenantId parameter.

parameters.name: notEnded
parameters.description: Set to true to only include tasks that are not completed or cancelled in the counts.

parameters.name: includeEventMetrics
parameters.description: Set to true to include the queue, completion, and rate metrics.

get.description: Retrieves the tasks in a queue that are not completed or cancelled, ordered with the highest priority first and, within each priority, oldest first. Requires the task-admin or task-reader role, or one of the worker or assigner roles of the queue. Core users with one of those roles can retrieve tasks using the tenantId parameter.

post.description: Creates a task in a queue of the tenant, with status Pending. Requires the task-admin or task-writer role. Core users with one of those roles can create tasks using the tenantId parameter. Also creates a comment topic for the task in the comment service.

get.description: Retrieves a task in a specified queue. Requires the task-admin or task-reader role, or one of the worker or assigner roles of the queue. Core users with one of those roles can retrieve the task using the tenantId parameter. Tasks of other tenants or other queues respond 404. Responds 400 without a tenant context.

patch.description: Updates a task in a specified queue. Requires the task-admin role, or the task-writer role together with a role that grants access to the task (task-reader, or a worker or assigner role of the queue), in the tenant of the task; core users can't update tasks. Tasks of other tenants or other queues respond 404.

post.description: Executes an operation on a task in a specified queue. The roles are the same as for POST /task/v1/tasks/{id}: the user must be able to access the task (the task-admin or task-reader role, or a worker or assigner role of the queue); assign requires the task-admin role or an assigner role, except that a worker can assign the task to themselves; set-priority requires the task-admin or task-writer role or an assigner role; start and complete require a worker role, and the task must be unassigned or assigned to the user; cancel is allowed for any user who can access the task. Tasks of other tenants or other queues respond 404. Responds 400 for an unrecognized operation, or when the task's status doesn't allow the operation.

patch.description: Replaces the data of a task in a specified queue. The task must be In Progress. Requires a worker role of the queue in the tenant of the task, and the task must be unassigned or assigned to the user. Tasks of other tenants or other queues respond 404.

get.description: Retrieves the users of the tenant's Keycloak realm that hold one of the worker roles of the queue. No task service role is required, but the request is made to the Keycloak admin API with the caller's token, so the user must hold the realm-management roles to view users (view-users) and, for client roles, clients (view-clients). Responds 403 if Keycloak denies the request. Roles that don't exist in the realm are skipped.

Retrieves tasks of the tenant across queues, ordered with the highest priority first and, within each priority, oldest first. Requires the task-admin or task-reader role in the tenant. Core users with the export-service export-job role (urn:ads:platform:export-service:export-job) can also retrieve tasks, using the tenantId parameter. Responds 400 without a tenant context.

parameters.name: criteria
parameters.description: JSON-encoded criteria to filter the tasks by. Must be valid JSON. Supported properties are queue (namespace and name), definition (namespace and name), context (tasks whose context contains these values), and notEnded (true to exclude completed and cancelled tasks).

get.description: Retrieves a specified task. Requires the task-admin or task-reader role, or one of the worker or assigner roles of the task's queue. Core users with one of those roles can retrieve the task using the tenantId parameter, as can the directory-service resource-resolver role (urn:ads:platform:directory-service:resource-resolver). Tasks of other tenants respond 404. Responds 400 without a tenant context.

patch.description: Updates a specified task. Requires the task-admin role, or the task-writer role together with a role that grants access to the task (task-reader, or a worker or assigner role of the queue), in the tenant of the task; core users can't update tasks. Tasks of other tenants respond 404.

post.description: Executes a task operation. The user must be able to access the task (the task-admin or task-reader role, or a worker or assigner role of the queue). Further roles depend on the operation, and are held in the tenant of the task: assign requires the task-admin role or an assigner role of the queue, except that a user with a worker role can assign the task to themselves; set-priority requires the task-admin or task-writer role or an assigner role; start and complete require a worker role of the queue, and the task must be unassigned or assigned to the user; cancel is allowed for any user who can access the task, that is with the task-admin or task-reader role or a worker or assigner role of the queue (core users with those roles included). Tasks of other tenants respond 404. Responds 400 for an unrecognized operation, or when the task's status doesn't allow the operation.

delete.description: Deletes a task. Requires the task-admin role in the tenant of the task; core users can't delete tasks. Tasks of other tenants respond 404.

patch.description: Replaces the data of a specified task. The task must be In Progress. Requires a worker role of the task's queue in the tenant of the task, and the task must be unassigned or assigned to the user. Tasks of other tenants respond 404.

TaskAfter.name: after
TaskAfter.description: Cursor of the page to retrieve. Use the `page.next` value of the previous response to page sequentially through the results.

TaskTenantId.name: tenantId
TaskTenantId.description: ID of the tenant to act on. Only used for core (platform) users; tenant users always act on the tenant of their token and this parameter is ignored. Core users must set it, since tasks and queues are scoped to a tenant.

TaskTop.name: top
TaskTop.description: Maximum number of tasks to return in the page.

QueueNotFound.description: Queue not found in the configuration of the tenant.

example.errorMessage: queue with ID 'support:intake-processing' could not be found.

QueuedTaskNotFound.description: Queue not found, or task not found in the queue of the tenant.

example.errorMessage: task with ID 'f3a3bc74-494e-4bb5-b5f3-d29a34edd275' could not be found.

TaskBadRequest.description: Request is invalid. For example, a path, query, or body parameter failed validation, there is no tenant context, or the operation is not valid for the task's status.

example.errorMessage: Validation failed with error(s): id (params) - Invalid value

TaskForbidden.description: User does not have a role required for the operation.

example.errorMessage: User Test User (ID: 3f0c7a2e-1b4d-4c8e-9a6f-2d5b8e1c7a90) not permitted to access task.

TaskNotFound.description: Task not found in the tenant (or, for a queue path, not found in that queue).

example.errorMessage: task with ID 'f3a3bc74-494e-4bb5-b5f3-d29a34edd275' could not be found.

TaskUnauthorized.description: Request does not include a valid bearer token.

AssignTask.description: Assigns the task to a user, or unassigns it when assignTo is omitted or null. Completed or cancelled tasks cannot be assigned.

CancelTask.description: Cancels a Pending or In Progress task.

reason.description: Indicates why the task was cancelled. Included in the task-cancelled event.

description.description: A short summary of the task to be performed.

recordId.description: An optional, application defined ID for cross-referencing purposes.

context.description: A JSON object used to provide an application-defined context for the task. Defaults to {}.

data.description: An optional, application-defined JSON object to further define the task. Defaults to {}.

definition.description: Optional application-defined task definition the task is created from.

priority.description: The task priority. Defaults to Normal.

namespace.description: The namespace in which the queue resides.

context.description: An application-defined JSON object to describe the context for the queue.

assignerRoles.description: Roles that allow a user to assign tasks in the queue to others, and to set task priority.

workerRoles.description: Roles that allow a user to assign themselves tasks in the queue, and to work on them.

namespace.description: The namespace in which the queue resides.

assignedTo.description: Number of tasks by assigned user, keyed by user ID.

queue.description: Weekly time in seconds tasks wait between created and started. Only set when includeEventMetrics is true.

completion.description: Weekly time in seconds tasks take between started and completed. Only set when includeEventMetrics is true.

rate.description: Number of tasks created, completed, and cancelled in the last 7 days. Only set when includeEventMetrics is true.

name.description: The user's first and last name, or username if the name isn't set.

SetTaskPriority.description: Used when setting a task's priority.

StartTask.description: Starts a Pending task, changing its status to In Progress.

Task.description: A task represents an action that a user must perform within a specified period of time.

id.description: Used to uniquely identify the task in the system. Generated when the task is created, use this ID in subsequent API calls.

description.description: A brief description of the task to be performed.
description.example: Please sign off on the completed IRC

queue.description: The queue to which the task has been submitted.

namespace.description: The namespace in which the queue resides.

definition.description: Optional application-defined task definition the task was created from.

recordId.description: An optional value for additional application defined context, such as the ID of a related record.

context.description: A JSON object used to provide an application-defined context for the task. Defaults to {}.

data.description: An optional, JSON object containing application-defined data to further define the task.

priority.description: Tasks can be prioritized in a queue. Higher priority tasks are pushed to the front.

status.description: Status of the task in its lifecycle. Changed by the start, complete, and cancel operations.

TaskAssignment.description: Tasks are assigned to users for completion. The assignment identifies who the task is assigned to, and who assigned it. assignedTo is null when the task was unassigned.

assignedTo.description: Identifies the user to which the task has been assigned by ID, name, and email address.

assignedBy.description: Identifies the user that assigned the task by ID, and name.

TaskData.description: Application-defined data to set on the task. Replaces the existing data.

deleted.description: Indicates whether the task was deleted.

after.description: Cursor representing the set of data returned.

next.description: Cursor representing the next set of data to be returned. Not set on the last page.

size.description: The number of tasks returned by the query.

TaskUpdate.description: Fields to update. Fields that are not included are left unchanged.

context.description: New task context. Replaces the existing context.

data.description: Application-defined JSON object to further define the task. Replaces the existing data.

priority.description: New priority for the task as a number, where 1 is Normal, 2 is High, and 3 is Urgent.
